correctness.rationale: All least-period-two solutions are reduced by two affine return equations and a unique z-coordinate solution to zero, equal or opposite x/y, or unequal squared x/y. For unequal squares, exact product and sum conditions are necessary and sufficient. Positivity and the distinct quadratic roots prove exact existence and multiplicity. Direct expansion of 3x3 return Jacobians with the orbit relation proves det(P-I)=2r(a²−b²)²/(1+r)>0 and thus an eigenvalue >1. The r=1/3 crossing follows by comparing exact thresholds. SymPy and rational checks complement, but do not replace, these universal derivations.

value.rationale: For the published canonical constant-Jacobian axial maps, the first nontrivial periodic-orbit population, its forced instability, and the precise order of symmetry-breaking births are structurally natural questions. The exact damping threshold r=1/3 separates a parameter interval with only two off-symmetry saddle cycles from a regime where a central cycle must appear first. The complete count and return-multiplier obstruction clarify periodic-organizing structures without relying on numerical attractor diagrams.
